text: In Grafana, open the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/ffz989fhtrqioa/fwgr73-n1-bench-dashboard. Do two things and make sure both are PERSISTED by explicitly saving: (1) Add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard (via Dashboard settings > General > Tags, add 'bench', then save the settings). (2) Set the dashboard's time range to 'Last 6 hours' using the time picker in the top bar, then click Save and in the save dialog TICK the 'Update default time range' checkbox before confirming the save, so the 6-hour range is stored in the saved dashboard. Then verify persistence: hard-reload the page and check Dashboard settings > General (or the JSON model) to confirm the tag 'bench' and the default time range of last 6 hours are actually stored in the saved dashboard. Report exactly what you observed for the tag and the stored default time range.

summary: Both changes were made and are persisted. (1) Tag: opened Edit > Settings > General, typed 'bench' in the Tags field and clicked Add — a chip 'Remove "bench" tag' appeared — then clicked Save dashboard. (2) Time range: the top-bar picker already read "Last 6 hours"; in the save drawer I ticked the 'Update default time range' checkbox and confirmed Save, which produced the "Dashboard saved" alert. Persistence verified after a hard reload of the URL with NO query parameters: Edit > Settings > JSON Model (now version 3) shows "tags": [ "bench" ] and "time": { "from": "now-6h", "to": "now" } (timepicker is empty, so the default comes from the top-level time field), and the reloaded page renders "Time range selected: Last 6 hours" with both panels 'fwgr73-n1 Notes' (text "Notes for run fwgr73-n1") and 'fwgr73-n1 Availability' (Stat, value 62.8). One caveat: a stray Ctrl+F attempt got typed into the Monaco JSON editor, overwriting its local buffer, but I navigated away without clicking "Save changes" and afterwards re-verified the stored model reads correctly (tags bench, time now-6h/now), so nothing was corrupted.
